content:
Welcome once again to my personal blog. This space on the web will share a little about my life here in Australia. I’m building it with Hugo, one of the most popular open-source static site generators. For the theme, I chose PaperMod. I like its clean style and lack of unnecessary frills.
From ChatGPT:
Static sites, such as those built with Hugo, offer many advantages over traditional CMS platforms like WordPress. Because they are generated directly as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, they deliver high performance, very fast load times, and a smoother browsing experience. They don’t require a database or server-side processing, which also makes them more secure, less exposed to attacks, and easier to maintain. They’re also easy to version and manage with Git, and can be published automatically using tools such as GitHub Actions. The result is a modern, lightweight, scalable, and affordable solution—ideal for anyone who wants a fast, reliable website that’s easy to maintain.

title: An invitation to you all

content:
As Aldo would say: “I can’t believe it!” And yes, on January 12, 2027, I’ll celebrate 20 years since arriving here in Australia.
I still remember it as if it were yesterday—well, to be honest, not quite—but I’ll try to tell you about it.
I arrived in Brisbane with lots of ideas, dreams to pursue, and a new life to plan.
It certainly wasn’t easy. There were many sacrifices to make and decisions to take, without a deep understanding of Australian institutions or familiar faces I could turn to for advice. But I had a solid plan: I was on the other side of the world to reinvent myself, and my first goal was to try to obtain citizenship. Eligibility was based on a points system calculated from factors such as education, age, and work experience.
I admit I had moments of discouragement, but in the end I never gave up. With the stubbornness of a true Bergamasco, I got there. I still had to graduate, complete another year of study through the ACS (Australian Computer Society), and do an internship. After that, I had enough points to apply for citizenship.
I’ll leave it there for now, but I’ll come back to this subject later.
